1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) that acts as an
6	**I/O bridge** between a Guitar Hero controller and an off-board host.
7	Five phototransistors above the TV strike line are sampled and streamed
8	out continuously; the host runs detection / chord / strum logic and
9	sends back a single-byte bitmask that drives the controller's button
10	GPIOs directly.
11	
12	In its `MARVIN_DRIVEN` mode the firmware contains **no game logic** — it only
13	scans ADCs, emits frames, and applies received bitmasks. A second build-time
14	mode, **`MODEL_DRIVEN`** (`FRETBOARD_MODE` in `main.c`, the current default),
15	makes the board standalone: an on-device int8 neural net (`model_infer.c`,
16	weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) maps the ADC window to the button
17	bitmask itself, no host required. SW0 toggles it; LED0 shows the state.
18	Inference runs in the main loop; the 240 Hz TC0 ISR only samples and applies.
19	See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and edge-ai
20	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md).
21	
22	## Hardware
23	
24	### Target
25	
26	| Spec | Value |
27	|------|-------|
28	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
29	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
30	| Clock | 24 MHz |
31	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
32	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
33	
34	### Pin Map
35	
36	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
37	
38	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
39	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
40	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
41	presence.
42	
43	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
44	|---------|-----------|-----|
45	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
46	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
47	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
48	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
49	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
50	
51	#### Button Outputs (Open-Drain GPIO)
52	
53	Each button output is normally tri-stated (input mode). To "press" a
54	button the pin is driven low (clear + output-enable). To "release" it
55	the pin returns to input mode, which floats the line and lets the
56	guitar controller's own pull-up restore the idle state.
57	
58	| Function | Pin | Cmd bit |
59	|----------|-----|---------|
60	| Green fret | PA06 | 0 |
61	| Red fret | PA05 | 1 |
62	| Yellow fret | PA07 | 2 |
63	| Blue fret | PA04 | 3 |
64	| Orange fret | PA01 | 4 |
65	| Strum down | PA03 | 5 |
66	| Strum up | PA00 | 6 |
67	
68	#### UART (SERCOM1)
69	
70	| Function | Pin |
71	|----------|-----|
72	| TX (data stream out) | PB00 |
73	| RX (command in) | PB01 |
74	
75	Baud: **500 000**, 8N1.
76	
77	## Software Architecture
78	
79	### Processing Loop
80	
81	`TC0` is configured to fire a periodic callback at **240 Hz**
82	(≈4.17 ms period). Each tick runs three stages in sequence from the
83	timer ISR:
84	
85	```
86	TC0 callback (240 Hz)
87	    |
88	    v
89	fret_scan_all()          Blocking ADC read of all 5 channels
90	    |
91	    v
92	data_stream_send()       17-byte frame over SERCOM1 TX
93	    |
94	    v
95	cmd_receive_update()     Drains SERCOM1 RX, applies latest bitmask
96	```
97	
98	`main()` is just init + idle loop; all work happens in the TC0 ISR.
99	
100	### Module Descriptions
101	
102	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
103	
104	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
105	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
106	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
107	
108	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
109	the firmware:
110	
111	```
112	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
113	```
114	
115	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
116	
117	Emits one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick over SERCOM1 TX:
118	
119	| Offset | Size | Field |
120	|-------:|-----:|-------|
121	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
122	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
123	| 3 | 2 | red |
124	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
125	| 7 | 2 | blue |
126	| 9 | 2 | orange |
127	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
128	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — actuator bitmask driven this scan |
129	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
130	
131	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames
132	dropped in transit (it advances per tick even when a send is skipped).
133	`applied_mask` is the bitmask `cmd_receive` currently drives, captured in the
134	same tick as the scan so sensor and actuator state are paired at the source
135	(used by edge-ai training-data export). The frame is dropped silently if the
136	TX free-buffer count is below the frame size. At 240 Hz this is 4 080 B/s —
137	well within the 50 000 B/s budget at 500 000 baud.
138	
139	#### cmd_receive ([cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [cmd_receive.h](cmd_receive.h))
140	
141	Drains the SERCOM1 RX buffer each tick. The **last byte received** in
142	the tick is interpreted as a button bitmask and applied directly:
143	
144	| Bit | Output |
145	|----:|--------|
146	| 0 | Green fret |
147	| 1 | Red fret |
148	| 2 | Yellow fret |
149	| 3 | Blue fret |
150	| 4 | Orange fret |
151	| 5 | Strum down |
152	| 6 | Strum up |
153	
154	Bit set → drive low (assert). Bit clear → tri-state (release).
155	
156	Note: only the most recent byte each tick is honoured. The host is
157	expected to send commands at a rate ≤ the loop rate; older bytes in
158	the same tick are coalesced away.
159	
160	## Tools
161	
162	### Host-side data-stream monitor
163	
164	[`tools/ds_monitor.py`](tools/ds_monitor.py) opens the serial port,
165	resyncs on `0x03 … 0xFC` framing, and reports actual frame rate, byte
166	rate, framing-error count, and current ADC values once per second.
167	
168	The script declares its dependencies inline (PEP 723) and is run via
169	[`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) — no manual venv or `pip install`
170	needed:
171	
172	```
173	./tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
174	# or, equivalently:
175	uv run tools/ds_monitor.py /dev/tty.usbmodem<...>
176	```
177	
178	Defaults: `--baud 500000 --expect-hz 240`.
179

186

189	| File | Purpose |
190	|------|---------|
191	| [main.c](main.c) | Init + TC0 callback wiring |
192	| [fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [.h](fret_scan.h) | ADC channel scanning |
193	| [data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [.h](data_stream.h) | UART output frame |
194	| [cmd_receive.c](cmd_receive.c) / [.h](cmd_receive.h) | UART input bitmask |
195	| [tools/ds_monitor.py](tools/ds_monitor.py) | Host-side frame-rate / content check |
196	| `fret_detect.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
197	| `fret_button.c` / `.h` | **Orphaned** (see [docs/journal.md](docs/journal.md)) |
198	| `fretboard-mcc/` | MCC Harmony peripheral libraries (generated) |
199

Good — I've got the fretboard link design and the LAN8651's interface model. Short answer up front: **yes, this is very feasible, and "fancy point-to-point UART with no Ethernet stack" is exactly the right mental model** — with one nuance about where the work actually lands.

## What the LAN8651B1 is

It's a **MAC-PHY**: it integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S PHY on-chip, and talks to the MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface") protocol. That's the whole reason it exists — to give a tiny MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link over 5 pins.

Critically, the chip does in hardware everything you'd think of as "the Ethernet hard parts":
- Line coding, PLCA/CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD
- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX** — you never compute a CRC
- Framing on the wire

So on the PIC32CM you are **not** writing an Ethernet MAC, and you definitely don't need TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack.

## What you *do* still need on the PIC32CM

Two layers, neither large:

1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + 2–3 GPIO (CS_N, IRQ_N, optionally RESET). You already use SERCOM1 for the UART; a free SERCOM covers this. Note: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on your 24 MHz part, not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling — irrelevant for your data rate.

2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — this is the only real "driver." The SPI link isn't byte-transparent like a UART; it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default 64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with credit-based flow control (TX credits / RX-chunks-available reported in each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference (`oa_tc6` / the OPEN Alliance "tc6-lib") that's small enough to run on an Arduino.

3. **A minimal L2 frame** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*, so you prepend a fixed 14-byte header (dest MAC, src MAC, ethertype) to your 17-byte payload and hand it over. That's it — no IP. For point-to-point you can hardcode two MACs (or broadcast) and a custom ethertype. Your 17-byte stream frame + 14-byte header = 31 bytes → fits in a single chunk; the 1-byte command likewise.

## Resource estimate on PIC32CM6408PL10 (64KB flash / 8KB SRAM)

| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Flash | **~6–10 KB** | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Drop the unused UART data path if you fully switch. |
| SRAM | **~1–2 KB** | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. Static, no malloc. Comfortable in 8 KB. |
| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | Free one available alongside SERCOM1. |
| GPIO | 2–3 | CS_N, IRQ_N (ext-int), optional RESET. |
| CPU | Negligible | At 240 Hz × ~31-byte frames, you push one chunk per tick. Interrupt-driven off IRQ_N; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |

Everything fits well inside your 64KB/8KB budget with room to spare, and it stays within your static-allocation rule.

## Verdict & the honest tradeoff

**Feasible: clearly yes.** You replace "write 17 bytes to a UART FIFO" with "build a 31-byte L2 frame and run one TC6 chunk transaction" — conceptually still point-to-point, no stack.

The cost you're trading for is **complexity**: the TC6 chunk/credit protocol is more involved than the current 2-wire UART, and it adds an SPI bus + an external IC + magnetics-free single-pair cabling. The current 500 kbaud UART already carries your 4 KB/s with ~12× headroom, so **bandwidth is not the reason to do this**. The reasons that *would* justify it:

- **Noise immunity & cable length** — differential single-pair Ethernet over a long, electrically hostile run to the guitar, vs. a TTL UART pair.
- **Multidrop** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair (future fretboards / sensors on a shared bus).
- Standard netdev on the marvin side **if marvin runs Linux** — then it's just a raw/UDP socket, near-zero new code there. If marvin is bare-metal/Harmony, it needs its own TC6 driver too — worth confirming before committing, since that doubles the firmware effort.

One thing I'd want to pin down: **does the marvin end run Linux?** That single fact decides whether the far side is "free" or a second driver port. Want me to check the marvin spec/journal for that, and/or log this evaluation as an open question in the fretboard journal?

Got it — and those two reasons change the calculus substantially. The "is it worth it over a working UART" caveat I raised is moot if PoDL and a T1S showcase are the actual goals; complexity is partly the point.

A few engineering notes on each:

## PoDL

This is arguably the strongest reason — **one twisted pair carries both the data and the fretboard's power**, so the cable to the guitar drops from "data pair + power pair + ground" to a single 2-wire link. Nice for a moving/awkwardly-cabled instrument.

Worth being precise about scope, though: **PoDL is not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only does data. PoDL is external coupling circuitry around the link:
- **PSE side (marvin):** a PoDL source controller + coupling inductors that inject DC onto the pair.
- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to the PIC32CM's rail.
- SACI/classification handshake if you want a managed PSE; for a fixed point-to-point pair you can run "dumb" PoDL with a fixed voltage and skip the negotiation.

So on the fretboard BOM this adds the PD coupling + a buck/LDO, but **zero additional MCU firmware** — PoDL is transparent to the PIC32CM. Your earlier resource budget (~6–10 KB flash, ~1–2 KB SRAM, one SERCOM-SPI + 2–3 GPIO) is unchanged. Microchip has reference PoDL designs that pair directly with the LAN865x EVBs, which also helps the demonstration story.

## T1S as a system demonstration

This reframes the whole thing: the goal isn't "cheapest link that moves 4 KB/s," it's "show 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a larger Microchip system." A few things that make the demo more compelling and are nearly free given you're already paying the TC6 cost:

- **Lean into PLCA/multidrop** rather than treating it as strict point-to-point — even a 2-node PLCA bus demonstrates the headline T1S feature (collision-free multidrop on one pair), and it leaves the door open to hanging a second sensor node or a future second fretboard on the same pair + same power.
- **Marvin runs bare-metal**, so it gets its own TC6 driver. You don't care about marvin's resources, but the upside is you'll have a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared between marvin and fretboard** — Cortex-A on marvin, Cortex-M0+ on fretboard — which is itself a tidy demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family.
- The link then visibly ties the whole stack together: SAM9X75 vision robot ⇄ T1S+PoDL single pair ⇄ PIC32CM I/O bridge. That's a clean Microchip-parts narrative (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM + PoDL).

## Net

Feasibility verdict stands — comfortably fits the PIC32CM PL10. The only real firmware cost is the shared OA TC6 chunk-protocol driver; PoDL is a BOM/board concern with no MCU footprint. Given the demo + PoDL motivation, I'd lean toward **PLCA multidrop from the start** rather than pure point-to-point, since it costs nothing extra and showcases the feature that actually distinguishes T1S.

Want me to capture this as a direction entry (open questions + rationale) in the fretboard journal — T1S/LAN8651 link, PoDL, PLCA-multidrop, shared TC6 driver — so it survives across sessions? Nothing's decided yet, so I'd file it as an exploration/decision-pending note rather than a locked decision.

Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
100	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.

```md
# fretboard ↔ marvin link — 10BASE-T1S + PoDL

Low-level design for moving the fretboard ↔ marvin link from a FLEXCOM2/SERCOM
UART pair to **10BASE-T1S single-pair Ethernet with "dumb" Power-over-Data-Lines
(PoDL)**. System-level summary and rationale live in [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md)
§6; this document holds the engineering detail.

Status: **direction, not yet built.** The link today is FLEXCOM2 UART (system
spec M2). Nothing here is flashed.

---

## 1. Why T1S here

- **PoDL** — one twisted pair carries both data *and* the fretboard's power, so
  the cable to the guitar is a single 2-wire link instead of a data pair plus a
  separate power feed. This is the primary motivation.
- **Robustness / reach** — differential single-pair Ethernet tolerates a long,
  electrically noisy run to a moving instrument better than a TTL UART pair.
- **Multidrop headroom** — 10BASE-T1S/PLCA puts up to 8 nodes on one pair, so a
  second sensor node or fretboard can share the same pair *and* the same power.
- **Demonstration** — showcasing 10BASE-T1S + PoDL doing real work inside a
  larger Microchip system (SAM9X7 + LAN8651 + PIC32CM) is an explicit goal, not
  just an incidental benefit. Bandwidth is *not* a motivation — the existing
  500 kbaud UART already carries the ~4 KB/s payload with ~12× headroom.

## 2. The part: LAN8651B1

A **MAC-PHY**: integrates the full IEEE 802.3 Clause 4 MAC *and* the 10BASE-T1S
PHY on one chip, and talks to the host MCU over **SPI** using the OPEN Alliance
TC6 ("10BASE-T1x MAC-PHY Serial Interface", v1.1) protocol. It exists precisely
to give a small MCU with no built-in Ethernet MAC a single-pair Ethernet link
over ~5 pins.

Done in hardware by the LAN8651 (the MCU never touches these):

- Line coding, PLCA / CSMA-CD media access, preamble/SFD.
- **FCS (CRC32) generation on TX and checking on RX.**
- On-wire framing and minimum-frame padding.

SPI: LAN8651 is an SPI client, SCLK up to 25 MHz. Pins: `SDI`, `SDO`, `CS_N`,
`SCLK`, `IRQ_N` (active-low interrupt), plus a reset.

## 3. What the host MCU must implement

No TCP/IP, ARP, DHCP, or any IP stack. Three layers, none large:

1. **SPI transport** — one SERCOM in SPI-master mode + GPIO for `CS_N`,
   `IRQ_N` (external interrupt), and reset.
2. **OA TC6 chunk protocol** — the only real "driver." Unlike a UART, the SPI
   link is *not* byte-transparent: it exchanges fixed-size **chunks** (default
   64-byte data payload + a 4-byte header on TX / 4-byte footer on RX), with
   credit-based flow control (TX credits and RX-chunks-available are reported in
   each footer), plus a separate control-transaction format for register
   read/writes during init. Microchip publishes an open-source reference
   (`oa_tc6` / the OPEN Alliance `tc6-lib`) small enough to run on an Arduino.
3. **Minimal L2 framing** — the MAC-PHY only transmits *valid Ethernet frames*,
   so the host prepends a fixed 14-byte Ethernet header (dest MAC, src MAC,
   ethertype) to the payload. For this link the MACs are hardcoded and a custom
   ethertype carries the existing frame formats verbatim:
   - fretboard → marvin: the 17-byte data-stream frame (see fretboard SPEC).
   - marvin → fretboard: the 1-byte button bitmask.

   17 B + 14 B header = 31 B → a single chunk. The 1-byte command likewise. The
   existing UART framing (`0x03 … 0xFC`, `sample_seq`, etc.) can ride unchanged
   inside the Ethernet payload, so higher layers don't need to know the
   transport changed.

## 4. Resource budget — fretboard (PIC32CM6408PL10048, 64 KB flash / 8 KB SRAM)

Estimates; static allocation only (no malloc), per project rule.

| Resource | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Flash | ~6–10 KB | OA TC6 lib (~4–8 KB) + SPI glue + L2 framing. Reclaim the UART data path if the UART link is fully retired. |
| SRAM | ~1–2 KB | A couple of chunk buffers + one TX/RX frame buffer. |
| SERCOM | 1 (SPI master) | A free SERCOM alongside SERCOM1 (still UART for now). |
| GPIO | 2–3 | `CS_N`, `IRQ_N` (ext-int), reset. |
| CPU | negligible | One chunk per 240 Hz tick, interrupt-driven off `IRQ_N`; the TC0 ISR stays lean. |

SPI clock: SERCOM SPI master maxes at GCLK/2 ≈ **12 MHz** on the 24 MHz part
(not the chip's 25 MHz ceiling) — irrelevant for this data rate.

Everything fits comfortably inside 64 KB / 8 KB.

## 5. marvin side

marvin runs **bare-metal (no Linux)**, so it does *not* get a free netdev — it
needs its own TC6 driver. The upside: a **single portable `oa_tc6` layer shared
between marvin (Cortex-A5) and fretboard (Cortex-M0+)**, which is itself a tidy
demonstration that the OPEN Alliance SPI driver scales across the family. marvin
resources are not a concern.

## 6. PoDL — "dumb" (no negotiation)

PoDL is **not in the LAN8651** — the MAC-PHY only moves data. PoDL is external
coupling circuitry around the pair, and it is **transparent to both MCUs** (zero
firmware footprint, the §4 budget is unaffected):

- **PSE side (marvin):** a fixed-voltage source + coupling inductors that inject
  DC onto the pair.
- **PD side (fretboard):** coupling inductors to extract DC + a regulator down to
  the PIC32CM rail.
- **Dumb / unmanaged:** no SCCP classification or negotiation handshake. Fixed
  supply voltage, fixed point-to-point pair, decided at design time. Simplest
  PoDL form; appropriate because the topology is fixed and both ends are ours.

Microchip has PoDL reference designs that pair with the LAN865x EVBs, which also
helps the demonstration story.

## 7. Topology: point-to-point vs PLCA multidrop

Recommended direction: **enable PLCA from the start** rather than strict
point-to-point. A 2-node PLCA bus already demonstrates the headline T1S feature
(collision-free multidrop on one pair) at no extra cost, and leaves the door
open to a second node sharing the same pair and power. Open until decided.

## 8. Open items

- PLCA vs pure point-to-point (see §7) — lean PLCA.
- PoDL supply voltage and the PD-side regulator topology (BOM, not firmware).
- Custom ethertype value and the two hardcoded MAC addresses.
- Whether to keep the UART link as a fallback during bring-up or cut over
  outright (affects whether SERCOM1's data path is reclaimed — §4).
- Magnetics-free coupling component selection on the Sensor-LCD5 PCB.

```

Live side-by-side comparison deferred. Format: dense `detector_state_t` records for all detectors + raw BGRX32 keyframes every 60 frames (1.38 MB/s sustained, comfortable on Class-10). No software JPEG (Cortex-A5 can't keep up; SAM9X75 has no HW encoder). Spec §4.6. |
56	| 2026-05-20 | `frame_epoch` (32-bit, incremented per captured ISC frame) is the master sync token across recordings, detectors, and any future off-board observers | Need single shared timeline; off-board detectors (e.g. Edge-AI device) record in their own format keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch` so post-hoc training-data alignment is trivial. Wraps after ~830 days @ 60 Hz. |
57	| 2026-05-20 | Operating modes are independent toggles (`detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`); named modes are presets over them | Matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split which has worked well in practice. Avoids a brittle global state machine. Spec §6. |
58	| 2026-05-01 | First real driver work is the TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI bridge | It's the gate between hardware-wired and pixels-in-memory. Everything downstream (vision, actuation) depends on it. |
59	| 2026-05-01 | Reference source = mainline Linux tc358743 driver + community 480p dumps | Linux driver has correct state machine / EDID / IRQ handling; community dumps have verified 480p register values. |
60	| 2026-05-01 | Integration shape (sensor vs standalone) deferred until Phase 3 | Avoid premature structure; real answer depends on how much state the driver actually needs. |
